dialog.body: Public Works, this is Kevin. How can I help you?
Hi Kevin. Yeah, hi, it's Neusa Spencer. I'm calling for my mother, she's out on Bliss Road, and I'm on speaker because I'm driving over there, so if I cut out, bear with me.
No problem, I can hear you fine. What's going on at your mother's place?

It's the water. The storm's been coming in since this morning, the one hitting today, and the driveway out front is holding a puddle again. Right at the apron where the driveway meets the street. And it doesn't go out to the street, it runs back down toward the garage door.
Okay, so the water's pooling at the bottom of the driveway and pitching toward the garage. Let me get that down. What's the address?
310 Bliss Road. Easton's Beach side, you know, down toward the old, um, the old bathhouse stand. Well, not the stand anymore, whatever's there now. Closer to the beach end anyway.
Three-ten Bliss Road, beach side. Got it. Is water in the garage yet?

Not yet as of when my mother called me at like ten. She said it's an inch or so from the door track. But it's been raining hard and the wind's going, and this is not the first time. Every decent storm it does this.
Every storm, okay. Have you reported it before?

Yes. A while back, I called, and somebody told me that stretch of Bliss Road is a state road. So it's not the city's problem, basically. Which, fine, but then whose is it? Because nobody's done anything, and the water is still sitting there.

Yeah, that's a fair question. Some of the roads out that way do belong to the state, and the drainage on them goes with that. I can't tell you offhand where the line is for the drain in front of your mom's house. Let me check with the supervisor and see whether it's ours or the state's.

See, that's the thing. Last time I got passed off and that was it. Nobody said call this number, nobody said we'll look. I'm tired of it, honestly. My mother is seventy-some years old and she's out there with a push broom in the rain.
I hear you. Tell her to stay inside if she can, the wind's no joke today. Let me ask a couple things so my notes are good. Is there a storm drain right there at the curb, do you know?
There's a grate, yeah, near the corner of the property. It's half covered with leaves and sand, the sand blows up from the beach. Whether it's clogged or just can't keep up, I couldn't tell you.
Sand and leaves, partly covered grate by the corner. That helps. And is the street itself flooded, or just the apron and driveway?

The street has water along the edge, but the driveway is the low spot. It's like a bowl. [pause] Sorry, I'm pulling onto, um, what do you call it, the road that used to go past the trolley, Memorial, Memorial Boulevard. Anyway I'm close.
No worries. I'm putting down: standing water at the driveway apron, running toward the garage, grate partially blocked, previous report told it's a state road. Does that sound right?
That's right. And I want that in there, the part about being told state road. So whoever reads it knows it's been brought up before.

It's in there. I can't promise a crew can get out today, with the storm going they're pretty stretched, mostly on the main roads and the emergency stuff. But I'll flag it so somebody looks at who owns that drain.

Okay. I get that they're busy. I just don't want it to be another thing where it falls through. I was going to be out running this morning, I'm training for a half marathon in the spring, and instead I'm spending my Friday on this.
Well, not the day for a long run anyway. Not with this wind off the water.
No, definitely not. [line breaks up] ...so anyway, can somebody call me back when it's done, or at least when you find out whose it is?
Absolutely. What's the best number?
It's 401-555-0156. That's my cell. If I don't pick up it's because I'm on the road or in the water with my mother's broom, just leave a message.
Four-oh-one, five-five-five, oh-one-five-six. Neusa Spencer. And that's a callback once it's been looked at, or once we know who's responsible.
Yes. Either one, honestly. I'd rather hear something than nothing.
Fair enough. One more thing, if the water does get into the garage or the house, call back right away, and if it gets dangerous, like it's rising fast or near any electrical, that's a call to 911.
Okay. Yeah. Her panel's in the garage actually, on the back wall. So that's, ugh. Okay. I'll keep an eye on it.
Then definitely keep her away from that area if the water comes up. I'll get this over to the supervisor right after we hang up so it's in front of them this afternoon.
Thank you, Kevin. I appreciate it. I'm just frustrated, it's been the same thing for years and I feel like I keep saying it to a wall.
Understood. You're not talking to a wall today, it's logged with your number. Drive safe over there.
Will do. Thanks. Bye.
Bye now.
